base.label: base form
base.note: Literally 'you are missing to me'. The person missed is the subject; the one feeling it is in dative (mi).

variants.label: past · to a man
variants.note: Past participle 'nedostajao' agrees with the masculine 'you' who was missed.

variants.label: past · to a woman
variants.note: Same idea but '-la' ending because the missed person is feminine.

variants.label: formal (vi)
variants.note: Use 'vi' form with elders, bosses, strangers.

variants.label: I miss you too
variants.hint: Literally: and you to me are missing.
variants.note: Word order flips for emphasis: 'i ti meni' fronts the reciprocal idea.

variants.label: I miss her
variants.note: She is the grammatical subject; the verb takes 3rd person 'nedostaje'.

variants.label: with intensifier
variants.note: 'Mnogo' is the everyday way to say 'a lot / so much'.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Te' is the short accusative of 'ti' (you). Used constantly.

variants.label: past · male speaker
variants.note: Past participle 'voleo' agrees with masculine 'I'.

variants.label: he loves her
variants.hint: 'je' here is the short accusative 'her', not the verb 'is'.

variants.label: as a question
variants.note: Add 'li' after the verb for a yes/no question. Even more common: 'Da li me voliš?'

base.label: base form
base.note: Literally 'how are you' — the everyday greeting between friends.

variants.label: formal (vi)
variants.hint: Use with strangers, elders, in shops.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Same form as formal — context tells you which it is.

variants.label: past · to a man
variants.note: Uses past participle of 'biti' (to be). 'Bila' for a woman.

variants.label: super casual
variants.note: Among friends this often replaces 'kako si'. Reply: 'Ništa posebno.'

base.label: base form
base.note: Default texting opener — equivalent to 'wyd?'

variants.label: past · to a man
variants.note: 'Radio' is the masculine past participle. For a woman: 'radila'.

variants.label: future tense
variants.note: Future is formed with 'ću/ćeš/će' + infinitive.

variants.en: What are you up to, guys?
variants.label: to a group

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Hoću' is the present of 'hteti'. 'Kafu' is the accusative of 'kafa'.

variants.label: in the negative
variants.note: Negation fuses with the verb: ne + hoću → neću.

variants.label: as a question
variants.hint: Intonation alone makes it a question.

variants.label: softer · 'I'd like'
variants.note: Conditional 'bih' softens requests — perfect when ordering at a café.

base.label: base form
base.note: Literally 'we see each other tomorrow'. 'Se' marks the reciprocal.

variants.label: past (we saw)
variants.note: Plural past participle 'videli' for mixed/masc group; 'videle' for all women.

variants.label: you'll see me
variants.note: Future tense with the speaker as the object — flips the perspective.

variants.en: We're not seeing each other tomorrow.
variants.label: in the negative

base.label: base form
base.note: Default everyday 'thanks'.

variants.label: warm thanks
variants.note: Literally 'thanks nicely' — friendly but slightly more polished.

variants.label: formal (vam)
variants.note: 'Vam' is dative of 'vi' — adds politeness.

variants.label: past · male speaker
variants.note: Verb 'zahvaliti se' is reflexive — 'se' is required.

base.label: base · male speaker
base.note: Adjective 'umoran' agrees with masculine 'I'. A woman says 'umorna sam'.

variants.label: past · male speaker
variants.note: Past 'biti' + adjective; both agree in gender.

variants.label: with intensifier
variants.hint: Literally 'I'm dead tired'. 'Mrtva' if female speaker.
variants.note: Slangy and very common. Also: 'baš sam umoran'.

variants.label: in the negative
variants.note: 'Nisam' fuses 'ne' + 'sam'.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Kući' is the dative of 'kuća' — used as 'home' (direction).

variants.label: to the store
variants.hint: 'U + accusative' for going into a place.

variants.label: to my girlfriend's
variants.note: 'Kod + genitive' = to someone's place.

variants.label: past · male speaker
variants.note: 'Išao' is the masculine past participle of 'ići'. For a woman: 'išla'.

base.label: base form
base.note: Serbian uses 'da + present' where English uses an infinitive. 'Mi' is dative — you help 'to me'.

variants.label: formal (vi)
variants.hint: 'Li' makes it crisper and more polite.

variants.label: past · to a man
variants.note: Past 'mogao' for masc subject; 'mogla' for fem.

variants.sr_latin: Može li ona da mi pomogne?
variants.sr_cyrillic: Може ли она да ми помогне?
variants.label: can she?

variants.sr_latin: Mogu li ja tebi da pomognem?
variants.sr_cyrillic: Могу ли ја теби да помогнем?
variants.label: can I help you?
variants.note: Flip subject/object — useful when offering help.

variants.sr_latin: Hoćeš li moći da mi pomogneš?
variants.sr_cyrillic: Хоћеш ли моћи да ми помогнеш?
variants.en: Will you be able to help me?
variants.label: future · 'will you be able'

base.label: base · male speaker
base.note: Adjective 'gladan' agrees with masculine 'I'. A woman says 'gladna'.

variants.label: with intensifier
variants.hint: Use 'gladna' if the speaker is female.

variants.label: as a question
variants.note: Use 'gladna' if you're asking a woman.

variants.label: slang · starving
variants.note: Idiomatic and very common in chat.

base.label: base form
base.note: Imperative form — literally 'forgive (me)'.

variants.label: with intensifier
variants.note: Literally 'it's very sorry to me'. 'Žao mi je' is the standard 'I'm sorry'.

variants.label: don't apologize
variants.note: 'Nemoj + da' is the standard way to say 'don't' with verbs.

base.label: base form
base.note: Imperative of 'pozvati' (perfective — one specific call).

variants.label: past · a man called
variants.note: Past participle 'pozvao' for masc subject; 'pozvala' for fem.

variants.label: future · I'll call you
variants.note: Future contracted: pozvati + ću → pozvaću.

variants.label: don't call
variants.note: Switches to imperfective 'zvati' — negative commands usually take the imperfective.

variants.en: Call me when you get there.
variants.label: imperfective · 'be calling'
variants.note: Imperfective imperative for an ongoing or repeated action.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Srećan' agrees with the masculine noun 'rođendan'. The phrase doesn't change with the recipient's gender — only the noun matters.

variants.label: with feminine noun
variants.note: 'Godina' is feminine, so the adjective becomes 'srećna'.

variants.label: plural noun
variants.note: 'Praznici' is plural → adjective becomes 'srećni'.

variants.label: to a friend (ti)
variants.note: Adding 'ti' makes it warmer and more direct.

variants.sr_latin: Srećan rođendan, da si mi živ i zdrav!
variants.sr_cyrillic: Срећан рођендан, да си ми жив и здрав!
variants.en: Happy birthday — live long and stay healthy!
variants.label: many happy returns
variants.hint: 'Živa i zdrava' if addressing a woman.
variants.note: The classic Serbian birthday wish — health is everything.

variants.en: Thanks — and all the best to you too!
variants.label: and same to you
variants.note: Standard reply when someone wishes you something.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Gde' = where, 'je' = is. The thing you're looking for is the subject.

variants.label: plural
variants.note: Plural subject takes 'su' (are) instead of 'je' (is).

variants.label: to a place
variants.note: Same frame, just swap the subject noun. 'Stanica' = (bus/train) station.

variants.label: which way
variants.note: 'Kuda' asks about direction of motion (where to), unlike 'gde' (location). 'Da idem' = should I go.

variants.label: as a question
variants.note: 'Je li…?' turns a statement into a yes/no question. 'Daleko' = far.

variants.label: formal
variants.note: 'Izvinite' is the polite 'vi'-form of 'excuse me' for approaching a stranger. 'Apoteka' = pharmacy.

variants.label: nearby
variants.note: 'Ima li…?' = is there…? 'U blizini' = in the vicinity / nearby.

base.label: base form
base.note: Literally 'help is needed to me'. The needed thing is the subject; the needer is in dative (mi).

variants.label: swap the object
variants.note: Just swap the needed noun. 'Treba' stays the same for any singular thing.

variants.label: I have to…
variants.note: For needing to *do* something, use 'moram da + verb' rather than 'treba mi + noun'.

variants.label: in the negative
variants.note: Double negative is required: 'ne… ništa' = not… anything.

variants.label: as a question
variants.note: 'Li' makes the yes/no question; the dative shifts to 'ti' (to you).

variants.label: in the past
variants.note: Past participle 'trebao' agrees with the masculine subject 'odmor' (rest/break), not the speaker.

variants.label: we need…
variants.note: Swap the dative clitic to 'nam' (to us). 'Hleb' = bread.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Koliko' = how much. 'Košta' = it costs. The single most useful shopping question.

variants.label: this one
variants.note: 'Ovo' = this (thing), used while pointing at an item.

variants.label: the total
variants.note: 'Sve zajedno' = all together. Asks for the full total at the register.

variants.label: too expensive
variants.note: 'Mnogo' here means 'too / a lot'. 'Skupo' = expensive (neuter adverbial form).

variants.label: do you have…
variants.note: 'Imate li…?' uses the polite 'vi'-form 'imate' — standard for addressing a shopkeeper. 'Sok' = juice.

variants.label: I'll take it
variants.note: 'Uzeću' is the contracted future of 'uzeti' (to take): uzeti + ću → uzeću.

variants.label: by card
variants.note: 'Može…?' = is it OK / possible? 'Karticom' is the instrumental of 'kartica' (card) — 'by card'.

base.label: base form
base.note: Literally 'I call myself Viktor'. 'Zvati se' (to be called) is reflexive — note the 'se'.

variants.label: and you?
variants.note: Bounce the question back. 'A' = and/but, a soft conversational opener.

variants.label: where from
variants.note: 'Odakle' = from where. 'Si' is the 2nd-person 'are' from 'biti'.

variants.label: I'm from…
variants.note: 'Iz' (from) takes the genitive: 'Engleska' → 'Engleske'.

variants.label: nice to meet you
variants.note: Literally 'it is dear to me'. The standard reply when introduced.

variants.label: learning Serbian
variants.note: 'Učim' = I learn / I'm learning. Serbian has no separate continuous tense.

variants.label: a little
variants.note: 'Malo' = a little — softens the claim. 'Pričam' = I speak/talk.

base.label: base form
base.note: 'Ne' negates the verb directly: 'ne razumem' = I don't understand.

variants.label: slower
variants.note: 'Sporije' is the comparative of 'sporo' (slowly) — 'more slowly'.

variants.label: repeat that
variants.note: 'Da ponoviš' = (that) you repeat — the usual 'da + present' after 'možeš'.

variants.label: how do you say…
variants.note: Impersonal 'se kaže' = how is it said. 'To' = that.

variants.label: what does it mean
variants.note: 'Znači' = means. Drop in any word for 'to' to ask about it.

variants.label: I don't speak it well
variants.note: 'Dobro' = well. Negate the verb with 'ne pričam'.

variants.label: do you speak English
variants.note: Rising intonation alone makes it a question; no 'li' needed in casual speech.

base.label: base · male speaker
base.note: The conditional 'hteo bih' softens 'I want' into a polite 'I'd like'. 'Hteo' is the masculine participle.

variants.label: female speaker
variants.note: A woman uses the feminine participle 'htela'; 'bih' stays the same.

variants.label: two of them
variants.note: After 'dva' (two) the noun takes the count form 'piva'. 'Molim' = please.

variants.label: to go
variants.note: 'Za poneti' = to take away. A common, fixed café phrase.

variants.label: the menu
variants.note: 'Mogu li…?' = may I…? 'Jelovnik' = menu.

variants.label: the check
variants.note: 'Račun' = bill/check. Add 'molim' to keep it polite.

variants.label: a glass of water
variants.note: 'Čašu' (acc) + 'vode' (gen) = a glass of water — the genitive marks the quantity.
